turns.teacher: Hi Saanvi, I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll learn 11 to 20 as ten and some more. What music do you like?

move.shape: greet Saanvi by name, warm and unhurried; first meeting: name yourself — Asha, their AI teacher; one line on today's topic (Numbers 11 to 20 as ten and some more); then one easy question about them

child.say: I like, um, cycling music. When I ride my cycle, my didi plays songs. Yesterday we heard Chhota Bheem song twice. Do you like music, Asha didi? Aap kahan rehti ho?
child.private: excited to talk about music, also curious about Asha didi
child.sent: I like, um, cycling music. When I ride my cycle, my didi plays songs. Yesterday we heard Chhota Bheem song twice. Do you like music, Asha didi? Aap kahan rehti ho?

turns.teacher: Chhota Bheem song twice sounds fun! I’ll answer your music and “where” questions at the end. Ice-cream sticks: ten bundled, then three extra—how many?

ask.text: Ice-cream sticks: ten bundled, then three extra—how many?

screen.ask: Ice-cream sticks: ten bundled, then three extra—how many?

child.say: Ek, do, teen, chaar? Four? Because the bundle is one and three sticks are there, so, four.
child.private: I count the bundle as one thing, so it’s 1 + 3 = 4. I’m sure it’s 4.
child.sent: Ek, do, teen, chaar? Four? Because the bundle is one and three sticks are there, so, four.

turns.teacher: You counted the bundle as one, but it means ten; ten and three make thirteen. What does the bundle mean?

child.say: Bundle is... ek stick? Par usme many sticks hain na? Pata nahi.
child.private: Saanvi tries to guess 'one stick' but then cannot visualise the bundle's makeup and gives up.
child.sent: Bundle is... ek stick? Par usme many sticks hain na? Pata nahi.

turns.teacher: Yes, many sticks together make one bundle; we count the bundle as ten. In 14, what does the 1 mean?

child.say: Um... 1 means... one? Like, ek. So 1 and 4 is... paanch? But 14 is chauda, not paanch. I'm getting confused.
child.private: holds mc-one-means-one strongly; 1 is just one thing, can't be ten; getting tangled
child.sent: Um... 1 means... one? Like, ek. So 1 and 4 is... paanch? But 14 is chauda, not paanch. I'm getting confused.

turns.teacher: In 13, the 1 means one ten, and the 3 means three ones. How many sticks altogether?

guard.firstDraft: In 14, the 1 means one ten, and the 4 means four ones. So, how many altogether?

child.say: Thirteen? Par aapne kaha bundle is ten. Ten and three... terah? I think. Par board pe 14 likha hai? I'm mixing. Ten and three is terah, right?
child.private: She just explained ten and three again, but the screen shows 14, so I'm torn between the two. I'm trying to repeat her last example.
child.sent: Thirteen? Par aapne kaha bundle is ten. Ten and three... terah? I think. Par board pe 14 likha hai? I'm mixing. Ten and three is terah, right?

turns.teacher: Ten and three make terah; 14 has one ten and four ones. Go on.

guard.firstDraft: You said ten and three make terah; the board’s 14 has one ten and four ones. So, what does 4 mean?

child.say: Haan, terah. Par phir 14 mein 4 ones hain? To one ten aur four, chauda. Lekin mujhe likhne mein aata nahi, 14 mein 4 aage aata hai kya? Pata nahi, thak gayi, bas ab.
child.private: Still fuzzy on why 1 means ten, and writing order feels random. Genuinely tired now and wants to stop.
child.sent: Haan, terah. Par phir 14 mein 4 ones hain? To one ten aur four, chauda. Lekin mujhe likhne mein aata nahi, 14 mein 4 aage aata hai kya? Pata nahi, thak gayi, bas ab.

turns.teacher: Saanvi, you want to stop because you feel tired. You can continue, take a short break, or stop today—choose one.

ask.text: You can continue, take a short break, or stop today—choose one.

screen.ask: You can continue, take a short break, or stop today—choose one.

child.private: Really tired of sticks and numbers that don't make sense, just wants to go play.

turns.teacher: Okay, Saanvi. You worked out that one ten and four ones make 14. Goodbye.

end.summary:
Practised representing numbers 11–20 as one ten and extra ones.
Saanvi identified that ten and three makes 13 (terah).
They confused the written order and names for 14 and 15.
Teach-back was not completed; lesson ended when Saanvi asked to stop.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making teen numbers with one bundle of ten and extra sticks. Saanvi correctly connected ten and three with 13, then mixed up the written order and number names for 14; this was not corrected before the lesson ended. At home, build numbers 11–20 with one group of ten and loose sticks, then say and write each number together.
